executive_summary.text: The Verizon 2026 DBIR reports exploited vulnerabilities now account for 31% of all breach initial access vectors (up from 20%), ransomware appears in 48% of breaches, and median patch time has risen to 43 days — signaling a structurally worsening enterprise security posture.

Microsoft dismantled Fox Tempest, a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that issued over 1,000 fraudulent 72-hour code-signing certificates via abused Microsoft Artifact Signing infrastructure, enabling ransomware groups including Rhysida, Vanilla Tempest, Qilin, and Akira to distribute malware as legitimate software.

The Mini Shai-Hulud worm-like malware (attributed to TeamPCP) has compromised approximately 600 npm packages — including AntV and TallyUI — by stealing maintainer tokens from infected developer environments and CI/CD pipelines, installing OS-level backdoors that survive package removal and poll GitHub for remote commands.

A CISA contractor publicly exposed AWS GovCloud credentials, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal systems, and SSH keys in a GitHub repository named 'Private-CISA'; the AWS keys remained valid for 48 hours after notification, representing one of the most severe government secret-exposure incidents on record.

A zero-day in on-premises Microsoft Exchange Server (CVE-2026-42897) is being actively exploited via crafted emails through Outlook Web Access with no patch yet available, while a public proof-of-concept for the Linux kernel DirtyDecrypt LPE (CVE-2026-31635) and a Windows zero-day dubbed MiniPlasma collectively underscore a simultaneous multi-platform privilege-escalation crisis.

cyber_news.title: Storm-2949 Abuses Microsoft SSPR to Execute Cloud-Wide Azure Breach Without Malware
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft documented Storm-2949, a threat actor that used social engineering to hijack accounts via Microsoft's Self-Service Password Reset feature, then leveraged the Microsoft Graph API for directory enumeration before exfiltrating data from OneDrive, SharePoint, Azure Key Vaults, Storage, and SQL databases. The actor also installed ScreenConnect on compromised VMs to maintain persistent access. The attack chain used no traditional malware, relying entirely on abused legitimate Microsoft tooling.
cyber_news.expanded: Storm-2949 initiated attacks by impersonating IT support staff and tricking users into approving fraudulent MFA prompts to complete SSPR takeovers, bypassing traditional credential-theft detection. After account compromise, the actor used the Microsoft Graph API — a legitimate service — to quietly enumerate the directory and identify high-value targets, making the activity difficult to distinguish from normal administrative behavior. Data exfiltration spanned multiple Azure services simultaneously, and ScreenConnect deployment provided a persistent remote foothold that survived password resets. The campaign demonstrates how identity-first cloud attacks can achieve full environment compromise without a single piece of custom malware, evading most endpoint-centric detection stacks.

cyber_news.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Worm Compromises 600 npm Packages via Stolen Maintainer Tokens
cyber_news.summary: The Mini Shai-Hulud malware (attributed to TeamPCP) has spread across approximately 600 npm packages — including AntV and TallyUI — by stealing maintainer authentication tokens from infected developer machines and CI/CD pipelines and publishing trojanized versions. The worm installs OS-level backdoors named kitty-monitor and gh-token-monitor that persist after package removal and poll GitHub for remote commands. A separate wave of copycat campaigns emerged after Shai-Hulud source code leaked publicly.
cyber_news.expanded: The worm propagates by harvesting npm tokens from compromised developer environments (including GitHub Actions runners), authenticating as legitimate package maintainers, and publishing poisoned package versions — a self-reinforcing supply chain infection loop. The installed backdoors (kitty-monitor, gh-token-monitor) are registered as system-level services or cron jobs, surviving both package uninstallation and OS reboots. The GitHub-polling command-and-control mechanism allows operators to push new payloads or exfiltration commands silently to all infected hosts. The public leak of the worm's source code has spawned multiple independent imitator campaigns with custom credential-stealing modifications, dramatically expanding the threat surface across the npm ecosystem.

cyber_news.title: GitHub Actions Supply Chain Attack Redirects Popular Tags to Credential-Stealing Commit
cyber_news.summary: Attackers manipulated popular GitHub Action tags to point to a malicious imposter commit designed to exfiltrate CI/CD pipeline secrets and credentials from any workflow consuming the affected actions. Organizations using the compromised actions by version tag rather than pinned commit SHA were exposed during the window of compromise. The attack is distinct from but contemporaneous with the Shai-Hulud npm campaign, indicating broad supply chain targeting of developer infrastructure.
cyber_news.expanded: GitHub Action tags are mutable Git references, meaning any repository consuming an action by tag name (e.g., uses: actions/checkout@v4) automatically runs whatever commit that tag currently points to. By moving a tag to a malicious commit, attackers gained arbitrary code execution inside victim CI/CD pipelines with access to all injected secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, cloud credentials, signing keys). This technique requires only write access to the upstream action repository — achievable via compromised maintainer accounts or via the Shai-Hulud token-theft loop. The attack mirrors the 2025 tj-actions/changed-files incident but demonstrates the technique remains viable and unmitigated at scale.

cyber_news.title: Microsoft Dismantles Fox Tempest Malware-Signing-as-a-Service Operation
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit disrupted Fox Tempest, which operated signspace[.]cloud — a commercial service selling fraudulent 72-hour code-signing certificates generated by abusing Microsoft Artifact Signing infrastructure — for up to $9,500 each to ransomware operators including Rhysida, Vanilla Tempest, INC, Qilin, and Akira. Over 1,000 fraudulent certificates were issued, enabling malware including Lumma Stealer, Oyster backdoor, and Vidar to masquerade as legitimately signed software. Microsoft evicted over 1,000 accounts and seized the signing infrastructure.
cyber_news.expanded: Fox Tempest exploited Microsoft's Artifact Signing service — designed for legitimate software publishers — by creating and cycling through Microsoft accounts to generate short-lived (72-hour) Authenticode certificates before detection and revocation could occur. The brief validity window was by design: ransomware payloads only needed to pass endpoint security inspection at initial execution, after which persistence mechanisms took over. By monetizing code-signing as a subscription service, Fox Tempest lowered the technical barrier for ransomware affiliates who lacked the infrastructure or reputation to obtain legitimate signing credentials independently. The operation illustrates how abuse of trusted vendor infrastructure — rather than custom exploit development — is now a core ransomware enablement commodity.

cyber_news.title: OAuth Consent Phishing Bypasses MFA by Harvesting Application Permissions Instead of Credentials
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors are abusing OAuth authorization flows to obtain persistent access to user accounts — including Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace — without ever capturing passwords or OTP codes, effectively rendering MFA irrelevant. By directing victims to legitimate OAuth consent screens for malicious or over-privileged applications, attackers receive access tokens that grant delegated permissions to mail, files, and contacts. The granted permissions persist even after password changes.
cyber_news.expanded: In OAuth consent phishing, the victim is presented with a legitimate-looking OAuth consent prompt (hosted on microsoft.com or accounts.google.com) for a registered malicious app — meaning the URL and certificate are genuine, defeating most phishing indicators. Once the user clicks 'Allow,' the attacker receives a refresh token providing long-lived API access scoped to whatever permissions were requested (mail read, file access, contacts). Because no credential or OTP is transmitted, hardware MFA tokens, number-matching push, and passkeys provide no protection against this vector. The attack is particularly effective against corporate environments where users are accustomed to approving OAuth consent for third-party integrations, and revocation requires administrators to actively audit and remove authorized application grants.

cyber_news.title: CISA Contractor Exposes AWS GovCloud Keys, Internal Passwords, and SSH Keys in Public GitHub Repo
cyber_news.summary: A CISA contractor published a GitHub repository named 'Private-CISA' containing AWS GovCloud credentials, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal CISA systems, and SSH keys — all publicly accessible. The AWS keys remained active for 48 hours after CISA was notified, providing a multi-day window for potential exfiltration of highly sensitive government data.
cyber_news.expanded: The repository name 'Private-CISA' suggests the contractor misunderstood GitHub repository visibility settings — a surprisingly common failure mode. The exposed AWS GovCloud credentials carried elevated privileges across multiple CISA internal systems, and the 48-hour remediation delay indicates either slow incident triage or bureaucratic friction in rotating production credentials for sensitive government infrastructure. Security researchers described the incident as among the most egregious government credential exposures on record, particularly given CISA's mandate to improve federal cybersecurity hygiene. The incident highlights the gap between CISA's public guidance on secrets management and its own operational security practices with third-party contractors.

cyber_news.title: Russian APT Turla Evolves Kazuar Backdoor Into Resilient Modular Peer-to-Peer Botnet
cyber_news.summary: Russian state APT group Turla has significantly retooled its long-running Kazuar backdoor into a modular peer-to-peer botnet architecture, dramatically increasing operational resilience and complicating takedown efforts. The evolution enables Turla to maintain persistent espionage access without relying on centralized C2 infrastructure that can be seized or sinkholed. Affected targets are consistent with Turla's historical focus on government, diplomatic, and defense organizations.
cyber_news.expanded: Classic Kazuar used centralized command-and-control servers that could be disrupted by domain seizure or sinkholing. The new P2P architecture distributes control across infected nodes — each peer can relay commands and exfiltrated data, meaning no single point of failure exists for law enforcement or defenders to exploit. The modular design allows Turla to push capability updates (new collection modules, evasion plugins) to implants without re-infection. P2P botnet architectures are associated with Tier-1 nation-state actors (e.g., Russia's Snake/Turla, China's Volt Typhoon) precisely because they maximize persistence and make attribution and remediation significantly more resource-intensive for defenders.

cyber_news.title: Verizon 2026 DBIR: Vulnerability Exploitation Surges to 31% of Initial Access, Patch Times Worsen
cyber_news.summary: Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found that exploited vulnerabilities are now the top known initial access vector at 31% (up from 20%), ransomware appears in 48% of all breaches, and median time to patch has risen to 43 days. Only 26% of CISA KEV vulnerabilities were fully remediated by organizations, indicating systemic patch management failures across industries.
cyber_news.expanded: The DBIR's vulnerability exploitation surge directly correlates with the proliferation of public PoC exploit code — a trend accelerated by AI-assisted exploit generation — compressing the window between CVE disclosure and weaponization below the industry's median patch cycle. The 43-day median patch time effectively means most organizations are routinely exposed to known, actively exploited vulnerabilities for over a month. The 26% CISA KEV remediation rate is particularly alarming given that KEV entries represent vulnerabilities with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation — the lowest bar for prioritization. Together, these metrics suggest the industry's vulnerability management capacity is not scaling with the volume and velocity of exploitation, a structural gap that ransomware operators are systematically monetizing.

cyber_news.title: INTERPOL Operation Ramz: 201 Arrested, 53 Servers Seized Across 13 MENA Countries
cyber_news.summary: INTERPOL's Operation Ramz concluded a four-month coordinated cybercrime crackdown across 13 Middle East and North Africa countries, resulting in 201 arrests, seizure of 53 servers running malware and phishing infrastructure, and identification of 382 additional suspects. Authorities also uncovered human trafficking operations in Jordan linked to scam call centers. Dismantled infrastructure included phishing platforms in Algeria and Morocco.
cyber_news.expanded: Operation Ramz is notable for uncovering the intersection of cybercrime and human trafficking — specifically forced labor in scam call centers, a model seen extensively in Southeast Asian pig-butchering operations now apparently replicated in MENA. The 53 seized servers supported a range of cybercrime services including phishing-as-a-service platforms, malware C2 infrastructure, and SMS spoofing systems used in bank fraud campaigns. The simultaneous multi-country coordination required real-time intelligence sharing across jurisdictions with historically limited cybercrime cooperation, suggesting improved INTERPOL liaison capacity in the region. The identification of 382 additional suspects beyond those arrested indicates ongoing prosecutorial work that may yield further infrastructure takedowns.

cyber_news.title: 47 Zero-Days Demonstrated at Pwn2Own Berlin for $1.3 Million in Awards
cyber_news.summary: Researchers uncovered 47 novel zero-day vulnerabilities across a wide range of modern software products at the Pwn2Own Berlin competition, earning $1.3 million in awards. The breadth of exploitable weaknesses demonstrated across enterprise and consumer software platforms underscores the continued gap between vendor security investment and attacker capability.
cyber_news.expanded: Pwn2Own results serve as a leading indicator for the vulnerability landscape: zero-days demonstrated at the competition typically appear in threat actor toolkits within 6-18 months as knowledge diffuses through the research community and details become public. The $1.3 million prize pool attracted top-tier researchers targeting operating systems, browsers, virtualization platforms, and enterprise software. The 47 vulnerability count in a single event is consistent with recent years and suggests neither vendor hardening nor secure-by-design initiatives have materially reduced the density of exploitable flaws in mainstream software. Several categories — virtualization escapes, kernel LPEs — are particularly relevant as building blocks for ransomware and APT attack chains.

deep_dive.title: Fox Tempest: How Malware-Signing-as-a-Service Is Industrializing Ransomware Delivery
deep_dive.content: Fox Tempest operated signspace[.]cloud as a commercial Malware-Signing-as-a-Service (MSaaS) platform, selling fraudulent 72-hour Authenticode code-signing certificates generated by systematically abusing Microsoft's legitimate Artifact Signing infrastructure. The threat actor cycled through over 1,000 Microsoft accounts to continuously obtain and re-generate certificates before Microsoft's abuse detection and revocation mechanisms could act — a velocity-based evasion strategy. Customers paid up to $9,500 per certificate and included ransomware groups Rhysida, Vanilla Tempest, INC, Qilin, and Akira, who used the certificates to make malware payloads including Lumma Stealer, Oyster backdoor, and Vidar appear as legitimately signed software — bypassing both Windows SmartScreen and enterprise endpoint security controls that rely on Authenticode trust chains. The 72-hour validity window was operationally sufficient: ransomware only needs to survive initial execution and establish persistence before certificate revocation becomes irrelevant. Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit responded by evicting all associated accounts, seizing the signspace[.]cloud infrastructure, and working with certificate authorities to revoke issued certificates. The operation illustrates the commoditization of previously high-barrier attack capabilities — code-signing infrastructure that once required significant resources and front company establishment is now available on a per-payload subscription basis, accelerating the democratization of ransomware deployment.

biggest_hacks.title: CISA Contractor Leaks AWS GovCloud Keys, Internal Credentials in Public GitHub Repository
biggest_hacks.summary: A CISA contractor inadvertently published AWS GovCloud credentials, dozens of plaintext internal passwords, and SSH keys in a public GitHub repository; the keys remained valid for 48 hours after notification, potentially exposing highly privileged U.S. government infrastructure.

biggest_hacks.title: Grafana Labs Confirms Source Code Stolen via GitHub Token Breach and Extortion Attempt
biggest_hacks.summary: Grafana Labs confirmed attackers breached a GitHub token, downloaded portions of the company's codebase, and then attempted to extort the company — raising concerns about potential supply chain risks for the widely deployed open-source observability platform.

biggest_hacks.title: 7-Eleven Confirms Data Breach Claimed by ShinyHunters
biggest_hacks.summary: 7-Eleven confirmed a data breach following claims by the ShinyHunters cybercriminal group, which is simultaneously conducting multiple extortion campaigns against major organizations.

biggest_hacks.title: B1ack's Stash Dark Web Marketplace Releases 4.6 Million Stolen Credit Cards for Free
biggest_hacks.summary: Dark web carding marketplace B1ack's Stash released 4.6 million stolen credit card records as a free download, dramatically expanding the pool of actionable fraud data available to low-tier cybercriminals.

biggest_hacks.title: Multiple U.S. Healthcare Organizations Breach Millions of Patient Records
biggest_hacks.summary: Several healthcare data breaches affecting hundreds of thousands to millions of patients were added to the HHS breach tracker, continuing the sector's status as the highest-impact target for data theft and ransomware.

vulnerabilities.product: Linux Kernel — DirtyDecrypt Local Privilege Escalation
vulnerabilities.description: Linux kernel LPE vulnerability with a public proof-of-concept exploit released, enabling local attackers to escalate to root. Patched in April 2026; PoC release elevates exploitation risk significantly.

vulnerabilities.product: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager
vulnerabilities.description: Authentication bypass allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to gain full administrative privileges. CISA Emergency Directive 26-03 applies; KEV due date was 2026-05-17.
Actively exploited vulnerability causing worker process crashes and potentially enabling remote code execution on affected NGINX web servers.

vulnerabilities.product: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (Captive Portal / User-ID Authentication Portal) — PA-Series, VM-Series
vulnerabilities.description: Out-of-bounds write enabling unauthenticated RCE with root privileges. CISA KEV listed 2026-05-06; patches released 2026-05-13.

vulnerabilities.product: Linux Kernel — Copy Fail Privilege Escalation
vulnerabilities.description: Incorrect resource transfer vulnerability in Linux kernel enabling privilege escalation. CISA KEV listed 2026-05-01; due date 2026-05-15. Impacts millions of Linux systems across distributions.
